newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Wednesday due to market uncertainty about their future trend, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,310 yuan ($398) per tonne, up 14 yuan. It opened at 3,300 and hit a low of 3,284.
January fell 10 to 3,230 yuan per tonne, March fell 30 to 3,240 and May rose seven to 3,217.
Combined volume rose to 19,200 tonnes from 8,400.
Traders said long and short position holders liquidated their positions because of the uncertain market trend.
"Many investors were cautious about the rises of the past few days," one trader said. "They thought it was a technical correction in thin volume after the heavy losses of the past weeks," he added.
"Soybean futures met strong resistance at high levels due to over-supply of spot soybean," a second trader said.
Analysts said there is limited potential for further rises in the next few days.
